newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia PM defends minister over job claims.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia PM defends minister over job claims.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Thursday defended Transport Minister John Sharp against allegations that he offered inducements to resign to a member of a government board, saying Sharp had acted sensibly.
"Can I say that I think John Sharp has adopted a commonsense approach," Howard told reporters.

On Wednesday, Sharp admitted in parliament that he had asked Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron to consider offering Gabi Hollows a position involved in aboriginal health if she resigned from the board of government air safety authority, the Civil Aviation Safety Authority.

"He (Sharp) is being criticised for trying to do the right and courteous thing by this particular person, and not in any way to call into doubt or question her credentials in other areas," Howard said.
He also said Sharp had been trying to lift the performance of the CASA board, which he believed had underperformed over a nunber of years.

On Wednesday, Howard said the Attorney-General's department had advised him that a letter from Herron to Hollows offering her an appointment in aboriginal health after her resignation from CASA was not in breach of the Crimes Act or other laws.
Howard has also said that Sharp's actions had not breached his code of ministerial conduct.
